input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV(I) lets Licensor unilaterally extend the Agreement for a further seven years, with no Licensee consent, no non-renewal right, no reminder, and no cap on renewal pricing. A unilateral multi-year extension is at or beyond our walk-away position (automatic multi-year renewals), and it contradicts Article IV(II)-(III), which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. The redline converts renewal to successive 12-month periods that Licensee may decline on 30 days' notice, requires a Licensor reminder 60 days before renewal, and caps renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, matching the preferred position; the fallback is renewal solely by mutual written agreement.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with 12-month renewals, 30-day Licensee opt-out, 60-day reminder and capped uplift
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year extension exercisable at Licensor's sole option, which also conflicts with Article IV(II)-(III) requiring extension by mutual written agreement. We have changed this to successive 12-month renewals that we may decline on 30 days' notice, with a 60-day renewal reminder and fee increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%; if preferred, we can instead simply provide that renewal occurs only by mutual written agreement.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: Following the Initial Period, this Agreement may be renewed for successive renewal periods of twelve (12) months each, provided that Licensee may elect not to renew by giving Licensor written notice no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current period, and Licensor shall notify Licensee of the upcoming renewal and any proposed fee change at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current period. Fees for any renewal period shall not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%) over the fees in effect during the immediately preceding period.
